help.text: What UMDF does
UMDF scans folders for duplicate photos, videos, audio and files. It combines exact byte comparison with perceptual fingerprints and scores which copy is most likely to be the original.
How detection works
• Exact: same size + SHA-256 (or full-file comparison) → 100%.
• Perceptual: the image is resampled to 75×75 grayscale; 'dpf' counts pixels within the gray tolerance.
• Video: ffprobe + one frame at 'Frame position', fingerprinted as an image.
• Audio: 5 s of decoded PCM hashed; re-muxed or retagged files match; lossy re-encoding does not.
Pixel tolerance (gray tolerance)

Maximum difference in gray level (0–255) for two pixels to count as equal. 0 = strict; 10 (default) tolerates JPEG recompression; 14–18 may tolerate local retouching; above ~24 false positives increase. It does not correct large crops or shifts.
If edited copies are missed, raise it gradually and review the results. For exact archives, lower it.
Metrics
• dpf (default): pixel tolerance; usually tolerates resize, compression and small retouching, but not large crops.
• ssim: global structural similarity; may tolerate local retouching better, but does not guarantee a match.
• sign: sign agreement of the normalised grid.
• pearson: correlation of the grids; stricter about structure.
• legacy: legacy sign-agreement metric kept for comparison; its scale is very permissive and it is not reliable for duplicate decisions.
• Semantic (optional): ONNX embeddings (ResNet/CLIP/SigLIP) compared by cosine. Disabled in standard builds; AI packages include it.
Semantic models (AI)
In an AI package, enable 'Semantic (AI)', press 'Models…', download a model and press 'Use'. The scan compares by embedding with cosine similarity; 'Similarity' sets the threshold.
ResNet-18/50: fast, general similarity for resized, recompressed or lightly edited photos.
CLIP/SigLIP: semantic scene/content similarity; they are not face recognition and do not identify people. The ~0.83 threshold is a model-dependent starting point.
Activating a model sets 'Similarity' to its recommended value (0.90 ResNet, 0.83 CLIP/SigLIP); tune it with your own photos.
Public models download without a token into the models folder (default ./models). Configuration lives in config.toml and the cache in cache.db.
AI packages bundle a CPU ONNX Runtime and default to CPU. For CUDA, point ORT_DYLIB_PATH at a GPU runtime and select CUDA; if it fails, CPU is used.
Recommended by case
Exact duplicates: SHA-256; no model needed.
Resized or recompressed: dpf (default) or ResNet embeddings.
Crops or different framing: CLIP/SigLIP may help, but the aspect-ratio gate (≤1.5) can exclude very different crops before comparison.
Same scene or content in different shots: CLIP/SigLIP with a ~0.83 starting threshold; review false positives.
Rotated: EXIF orientation is applied; a rotation baked into the pixels without EXIF can be missed even by semantic models. Review it manually.
Red-eye or local retouching: try dpf with tolerance 14–18 or ssim; otherwise review manually. Raising the tolerance increases false positives.
Video: one frame at 'Frame position'; audio: 5 s of PCM. Requires ffmpeg and ffprobe on PATH.
Rotated and edited photos
• EXIF orientation is applied when decoding: a tagged photo matches its physically rotated copy.
• A rotation applied to the pixels without EXIF may not be detected; there is no guarantee, so review it manually.
• Red-eye correction changes a small area; dpf/ssim may still match, but it is not guaranteed. Adjust tolerance or threshold and verify.
Which copy is kept?

The 'original' policy computes a heuristic score from resolution, bytes per pixel, age, EXIF richness, name markers and location. It is not a probability and does not guarantee the original; the preview shows the score and reasons.
Safe actions
• Trash/Move/Delete act on one duplicate; bulk buttons ask for confirmation.
• Trash depends on the desktop and filesystem; Delete is permanent and irreversible.
• After deleting, the next row stays selected to compare and delete repeatedly.
• Keyboard: ↑/↓ select, Del/Delete removes.
Performance
Decoding, hashing and comparison use all CPUs by default; adjust 'Threads' or --threads. Perceptual comparison is O(n²) in the worst case and large images consume memory.
Limitations
• The 'original' score is heuristic: it ranks candidates, it does not guarantee which copy is the original.
• The 75×75 grayscale grid can fail on very dark, low-contrast or mostly uniform images.
• The aspect-ratio gate (max/min ≤ 1.5) can discard very different crops or framings.
• dpf tolerates recompression and small changes, not large crops or baked-in rotations; raising the tolerance increases false positives.
• CLIP/SigLIP compare global content, not faces or identity; different people in similar scenes can match.
• The 0.90/0.83 thresholds are starting points that depend on the model and the collection.
• Video: a single frame; a different frame, cut or duration may not be detected.
• Audio: re-muxing/retagging matches; lossy re-encoding does not.
• Without ffmpeg/ffprobe only images and exact files are compared.
• Corrupt, unsupported or very large files may be skipped or consume a lot of memory.
• Trash/Move depend on the system; Delete is irreversible.
• Standard builds have no embeddings; AI packages bundle a CPU runtime. CUDA requires an external GPU ONNX Runtime (ORT_DYLIB_PATH).
• Downloaded models are not included in the installer and keep the license of their upstream repository.
